description_en: Between 2025-05 and 2025-12, thephalcawas rebuilt from ground-up with new materials. The whereabouts of the last historic column, one inscription and the Garuḍa statue, which were documented in 2020, are not known.Following is the description written in 2020 during the first documentation by the DANAM team:Very little of this historic 17th centuryphalcāremains since it was rebuilt with brick and concrete. Most of the original three-bayphalcāhas been replaced with a brick and concrete structure and only a few historic fragments survive. Two-thirds of thephalcāwere converted into a shop selling newspapers with new brick and cement walls and closed off by steel shutters. The traditional roof was recently replaced with a concrete slab. One carved wooden pillar, fragments of the east and north-facing walls and two shrines are the only historical materials that remain today.B. Basukala & Gutschow(2018) have dated the wooden pillar to ca.1700 CE.There are five inscriptions in thephalcā- two are embedded in the northern wall and three in the eastern wall. None of them provides information about thephalcā's initial construction. One of the inscriptions embedded in the northern wall is dated NS 803 (1683 CE) and names thephalcāas Bāde Phale and the area as Bādephale Ṭola. The inscription also mentions that a platform paved withteliyābricks was built to serve as a place for the five noble village elders (Pañcasamūha) to hold their meetings. It can be assumed that the elders met on the platform in front of thephalcāto discuss local disputes. The second inscription embedded in the northern wall informs that a niche was established and framed with a woodentoraṇain NS 806 (1686 CE). The three inscriptions embedded in the eastern wall are dated NS 839, VS 1946 and VS 2041; they all relate various restoration works on thephalcā.Local people worship the Gaṇeśa residing in thephalcāas their local deity (sthānagaṇeśa). Theguṭhīrelated to thephalcāorganises an annual worship on the 4th day of the dark fortnight of Pauṣa. According to aguṭhīmember, the rent collected from the shopkeeper covers the expenses for this ritual. However, the shopkeeper has claimed ownership of thephalcā​​​​​​​ and is currently engaged in a legal dispute with theguṭhī.
description_ne: यो फल्चा हाल पसल र गणेशको देवस्थल गरी दुई हिस्सामा विभक्त छ । फल्चाको तीन भागको दुई भागमा सटर निकाली पसल खोलिएको छ भने बाँकी हिस्सामा गणेशको देवस्थलका रूपमा खुल्ला छाडिएको छ ।यो फल्चाको प्रारम्भिक निर्माणबारे जान्न सकिने कुनै अभिलेख प्राप्त छैन । फल्चामा भएको नेसं ८०३ को अभिलेखमा यसलाई ‘बादे फले’ भनिएको छ र फल्चा अवस्थित यस स्थानलाई ‘बादेफले टोल’ बताइएको छ । यसबाट नेसं ८०३ सम्ममा यसै फल्चाको नामबाट पुरै टोललाई जनाउने स्थाननाम स्थापित भैसकेको देखिन्छ । सोही अभिलेखमा फल्चा अगाडि तेलिया इँट छापी पञ्चसमूह बस्ने ठाउँ बनाइएको प्रसंग छ । यसबाट मध्यकालमा यो फल्चा अगाडि पञ्चहरूको समूह बसी सामाजिक मुद्दा मामिलामा छलफल हुने परम्परा थियो कि भन्ने अनुमान हुन्छ । फल्चाको उत्तरी भित्तामा काष्ठतोरणबाट सजाइएको गवाक्षमा गणेशको मूर्ति राखिएको छ । उक्त गणेशलाई नेसं ८०६ मा तोरण चढाइएको अभिलेख प्राप्त भएबाट फल्चामा मध्यकालदेखि नै गणेश मूर्ति पनि रहँदै आएको थाहा हुन्छ । यस फल्चाको जीर्णोद्धार नेसं ८३९, विसं १९४६ र विसं २०४१ मा गरिएको तथ्य खुल्ने शिलापत्रहरू फल्चामा टाँसिएका छन् । तीन कवल भएको, परम्परागत वास्तुशैलीमा निर्मित फल्चालाई विसं २०४१ सालमा गरिएको पुनःनिर्माणका क्रममा सिमेन्टको संरचनामा रूपान्तरण गरिएको हो । फल्चाको पूर्वी कुनातिर पुरानो अवशेषका रूपमा बचेको एकमात्र थामो खडा छ जसलाई सन् १७०० तिरको मानिएको छ (B. Basukala & Gutschow2018) ।उक्त गणेशलाई यस टोलका वासिन्दाले थान गणेशका रूपमा पूज्दै आएका छन् । श्रेष्ठ समुदायको एउटा गुठी यस गणेशथानसँग सम्बन्धित छ । उक्त गुठीले पौष कृष्ण चौथीका दिन गणेशलाई बोको बलि दिएर पूजा गरी भोज खाने परम्परा छ । गुठीको यस वार्षिक कर्म फल्चाकै आधा भागमा खोलिएको पसलको भाडा (आय)ले धान्दै आएको भनाइ गुठीका एक सदस्यको छ । तर लामो समयदेखि त्यहाँ बस्दै आएका पसले सो गुठीसँग फल्चाको हक लाग्ने कागजात नभएको भन्दै गुठीले अनाधिकृत रूपमा भाडा उठाउँदै आएको बताउछन् । फल्चाको स्वामित्वको सन्दर्भमा हाल पसले र गुठीयार दुबै पक्ष कानुनी प्रक्रियामा लागिपरेका छन् ।

historical_events.event_description: A platform paved with terracotta bricks (teliyā) was constructed to serve as a venue for meetings of the five village elders (pañcasamūha). It can be assumed that such meetings took place in front of thephalcāduring the late Malla period, where elders convened to resolve local disputes.
A woodentoraṇawas added to the Gaṇeśa shrine by Bābu Siṃha Bhāro of Svahanani Ṭola.
Thephalcā'srestoration was commissioned by six individuals: Gopīrāja, Hāku, Vasūdeva, Motirāja, Lakṣmīsiṃha and Suṣuri.

Following its collapse, thephalcāwas restored in VS 1946 by Siddhisudharamātyaya from Bāliphaḥ Ṭola and Ratnakumāra Śreṣṭha from Nabahā Nani. Theguṭhīmembers did not contribute to the restoration. The inscription further stipulates that while any donor may restore thephalcā, no one may claim it as their property.
Parts of thephalcāwere replaced with brick walls and a slab on top. Members of theguṭhirebuilt thephalcāunder the guidance of Ṭākura Māna Śreṣṭha, a senior member of Cauthī Guṭhī.
